objects.description: Opaque handle to an open sound file. Acts similarly to FILE* from stdio; used with libsndfile read/write/seek APIs. The actual struct is private to the library.
Signed 64-bit integer type used for frame/item counts, offsets, and sizes within libsndfile. Range is typically INT64_MAX; macro SF_COUNT_MAX defines the maximum.

Structure describing the format and stream parameters of a sound file. Passed to sf_open* for input (on write) and filled by the library (on read). Fields: total frames, sample rate, channel count, format bitfield, number of sections, and whether the file is seekable.
Describes a file format or subtype supported by libsndfile. Used with sf_command and SFC_GET_FORMAT_* queries to enumerate formats/subtypes and their names/extensions.
Reserved-for-future dither configuration structure. Contains dither type, level, and a descriptive name. Some SFC_* dither commands exist but dithering is not implemented per comments.
Describes an embedded file region within a larger file: byte offset and length. Used with SFC_GET_EMBED_FILE_INFO.
Represents a single cue/marker within an audio file, including identifier, position, chunk metadata, sample offset, and a name string.
Fixed-size container for up to 100 cue points. Field cue_count indicates valid entries; cue_points holds the array. Macro SF_CUES_VAR allows other sizes for custom use.
Instrument metadata, including gain, base note, detune, key/velocity ranges, and up to 16 loops (each with mode, start/end, and repeat count). Used with SFC_GET/SET_INSTRUMENT.
Loop and tempo-related metadata: time signature, loop mode, number of beats, BPM, root MIDI key, and reserved fields. Used with SFC_GET_LOOP_INFO.

objects.definition:
#define	SF_BROADCAST_INFO_VAR(coding_hist_size) \
			struct \
			{	char		description [256] ; \
				char		originator [32] ; \
				char		originator_reference [32] ; \
				char		origination_date [10] ; \
				char		origination_time [8] ; \
				uint32_t	time_reference_low ; \
				uint32_t	time_reference_high ; \
				short		version ; \
				char		umid [64] ; \
				int16_t	loudness_value ; \
				int16_t	loudness_range ; \
				int16_t	max_true_peak_level ; \
				int16_t	max_momentary_loudness ; \
				int16_t	max_shortterm_loudness ; \
				char		reserved [180] ; \
				uint32_t	coding_history_size ; \
				char		coding_history [coding_hist_size] ; \

/* SF_BROADCAST_INFO is the above struct with coding_history field of 256 bytes. */
typedef SF_BROADCAST_INFO_VAR (256) SF_BROADCAST_INFO ;
objects.description: Broadcast (EBU bext) metadata block used mainly by WAV/BWAV. Contains description, originator, timestamps, UMID, loudness metrics, reserved bytes, and coding history (256 bytes here; macro allows other sizes).
Represents a single CART timer entry (usage code and value). Used inside SF_CART_INFO.

#define	SF_CART_INFO_VAR(p_tag_text_size) \
			struct \
			{	char		version [4] ; \
				char		title [64] ; \
				char		artist [64] ; \
				char		cut_id [64] ; \
				char		client_id [64] ; \
				char		category [64] ; \
				char		classification [64] ; \
				char		out_cue [64] ; \

objects.description: CART chunk metadata structure for radio automation. Contains descriptive fields, timers, URL, and a tag_text area (256 bytes here; macro allows other sizes). Used with SFC_GET/SET_CART_INFO.
Callback table for virtual I/O: user-provided functions to get length, seek, read, write, and tell. Passed to sf_open_virtual to access data sources other than standard file descriptors.
Describes a generic file chunk (ID bytes, ID length, data length, and data pointer). Used with sf_set_chunk and chunk iterator APIs to set/get arbitrary format chunks.
Opaque iterator over chunks in a file for use with sf_get_chunk_iterator, sf_next_chunk_iterator, sf_get_chunk_size, and sf_get_chunk_data. The underlying structure is private to the library.

C++ RAII wrapper for libsndfile’s SNDFILE*. Manages lifetime through an internal reference-counted holder SNDFILE_ref, exposes convenient constructors for paths, fds, and virtual I/O, and forwards operations for read/write/seek/metadata. Copyable, movable, and implicitly convertible to bool for validity checks.

functions.name: sf_open
functions.signature: SNDFILE* sf_open(const char *path, int mode, SF_INFO *sfinfo)
functions.description: Opens an audio file for reading, writing, or read/write using libsndfile. On success returns an opaque SNDFILE* handle and fills sfinfo; on error returns NULL and the error string can be obtained with sf_strerror(NULL). Intended usage: set SF_INFO (format/channels/samplerate) for writing; for reading, pass an allocated SF_INFO (fields will be filled). Must be closed with sf_close().
requirements: path must be a valid, null-terminated filename string.
mode must be one of SFM_READ, SFM_WRITE, or SFM_RDWR.
sfinfo must be a valid, non-NULL pointer.
When opening for writing, sfinfo->format, sfinfo->channels, and sfinfo->samplerate must describe a valid combination (use sf_format_check).
All successful sf_open() calls must be matched by sf_close() on the returned handle.
On error, retrieve the error string via sf_strerror(NULL).

functions.name: sf_open_fd
functions.signature: SNDFILE* sf_open_fd(int fd, int mode, SF_INFO *sfinfo, int close_desc)
functions.description: Creates an SNDFILE* from an existing file descriptor. Assumes the file header starts at the current file offset (useful for embedded files). If close_desc is non-zero, the file descriptor will be closed when sf_close() is called; otherwise it remains open.
requirements: fd must be a valid, open file descriptor positioned at the start of the file header.
mode must be one of SFM_READ, SFM_WRITE, or SFM_RDWR.
sfinfo must be a valid, non-NULL pointer.
When opening for writing, sfinfo fields must describe a valid format/channels/samplerate combination (use sf_format_check).
All successful sf_open_fd() calls must be matched by sf_close().
close_desc controls whether the original descriptor is closed by sf_close() (non-zero=close, zero=leave open).

functions.name: sf_open_virtual
functions.signature: SNDFILE* sf_open_virtual(SF_VIRTUAL_IO *sfvirtual, int mode, SF_INFO *sfinfo, void *user_data)
functions.description: Opens a virtual audio stream using user-provided I/O callbacks (SF_VIRTUAL_IO) instead of a real file. Returns an SNDFILE* on success, NULL on error. The callbacks will be used for all I/O.
requirements: sfvirtual must be a valid pointer to a struct with appropriate function pointers set for the chosen mode (read callbacks for reading; write callbacks for writing).
mode must be SFM_READ, SFM_WRITE, or SFM_RDWR.
sfinfo must be non-NULL; for writing, supply valid format/channels/samplerate; for reading, it will be filled.
user_data is passed to the callbacks and may be NULL if callbacks do not use it.
All successful calls must be matched by sf_close().

functions.name: sf_error
functions.description: Returns the current error code for the given SNDFILE handle. Use sf_error_number() to translate the code to a string, or sf_strerror(sndfile) to get the message.
requirements: sndfile must be a valid SNDFILE* obtained from a successful open function.

functions.name: sf_strerror
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the current error message string for the given SNDFILE. Passing NULL returns the most recent library error message (as used after sf_open failure). The returned string is owned by the library.
requirements: sndfile may be NULL (to get a global/last error) or a valid SNDFILE*.
Caller must not modify or free the returned string.

functions.name: sf_error_number
functions.description: Returns a constant error message string corresponding to the given error code.
requirements: errnum should be one of the public error values (e.g., SF_ERR_*) for meaningful results.
Caller must not modify or free the returned string.

functions.name: sf_perror
functions.description: Deprecated. Prints the current error message for the given SNDFILE to stderr and returns an int status. Prefer sf_strerror().
requirements: sndfile should be a valid SNDFILE*.
Being deprecated, new code should avoid relying on this function.

functions.name: sf_error_str
functions.signature: int sf_error_str(SNDFILE *sndfile, char* str, size_t len)
functions.description: Deprecated. Writes the current error message for sndfile into the caller-provided buffer. Prefer sf_strerror().
requirements: sndfile should be a valid SNDFILE*.
str must point to a writable buffer of at least len bytes.
len must be the size of the buffer; should be > 0.

functions.name: sf_command
functions.signature: int sf_command(SNDFILE *sndfile, int command, void *data, int datasize)
functions.description: Library control/query interface for miscellaneous operations (format info, normalization, metadata, encoding options, etc.). The semantics of data and datasize depend on the command (SFC_*). Returns 0 or SF_ERR_NO_ERROR on success, non-zero on failure depending on command.
requirements: sndfile must be a valid SNDFILE* (some commands may allow NULL but this header does not specify such usage).
command must be one of the SFC_* constants defined in this header.
data must point to the appropriate structure or value type required by the command (see each SFC_* documentation).
datasize must match the size expected for the given command.
Caller must ensure command-specific preconditions (e.g., only callable for certain formats or open modes).

functions.name: sf_format_check
functions.description: Validates that the combination of fields in an SF_INFO struct (format, channels, samplerate) is supported. Returns non-zero if valid, 0 otherwise.
requirements: info must be a valid, non-NULL pointer.
info->format, info->channels, and info->samplerate should be set to desired values before calling.

functions.name: sf_seek
functions.signature: sf_count_t sf_seek(SNDFILE *sndfile, sf_count_t frames, int whence)
functions.description: Seeks the read/write position within the audio data section. whence is like fseek (SF_SEEK_SET, SF_SEEK_CUR, SF_SEEK_END). Returns new position in frames from start on success, or -1 on error.
requirements: sndfile must be a valid SNDFILE*.
whence must be SF_SEEK_SET, SF_SEEK_CUR, or SF_SEEK_END.
frames is the frame offset relative to whence; may be negative only when used with SF_SEEK_CUR or SF_SEEK_END when supported by the format.
On files opened SFM_RDWR, see documentation for read vs write pointer behavior.

functions.name: sf_set_string
functions.signature: int sf_set_string(SNDFILE *sndfile, int str_type, const char* str)
functions.description: Sets a text metadata field (title, artist, etc.) on the file, if supported by its format. Returns 0 on success, non-zero on error.
requirements: sndfile must be a valid, open SNDFILE*.
str_type must be one of SF_STR_* constants supported by the file format.
str must be a valid, null-terminated string.
Not all formats or fields are supported; setting unsupported fields will fail.

functions.name: sf_get_string
functions.description: Retrieves a text metadata field from the file. Returns a pointer to the string, or NULL if unsupported or not present.
requirements: sndfile must be a valid SNDFILE*.
str_type must be one of the SF_STR_* constants.
Caller must not modify or free the returned string.
Returned pointer remains valid at least until the file is closed.

functions.name: sf_version_string
functions.description: Returns a constant string identifying the libsndfile library version.
requirements: Caller must not modify or free the returned string.

functions.name: sf_current_byterate
functions.description: Returns the current byterate (bytes per second) of the audio data at the current point in the file. May be accurate, approximate, or time-varying depending on the format. Returns -1 if unknown.
requirements: sndfile must be a valid SNDFILE*.
Interpretation depends on format; to get bitrate in bits/s, multiply by 8.

functions.name: sf_read_raw
functions.description: Reads raw data bytes from the file into ptr without conversion. Returns number of bytes read.
requirements: sndfile must be valid and opened for reading (SFM_READ or SFM_RDWR).
ptr must point to a writable buffer of at least bytes bytes.
bytes must be >= 0.

functions.name: sf_write_raw
functions.signature: sf_count_t sf_write_raw(SNDFILE *sndfile, const void *ptr, sf_count_t bytes)
functions.description: Writes raw data bytes from ptr to the file without conversion. Returns number of bytes written.
requirements: sndfile must be valid and opened for writing (SFM_WRITE or SFM_RDWR).
ptr must point to a readable buffer of at least bytes bytes.
bytes must be >= 0.

functions.name: sf_readf_short
functions.description: Reads up to frames frames, converting to native short samples, interleaved by channel. Returns frames actually read.
requirements: sndfile must be valid and opened for reading.
ptr must be a writable buffer with space for frames * channels samples.
frames must be >= 0.

functions.name: sf_writef_short
functions.signature: sf_count_t sf_writef_short(SNDFILE *sndfile, const short *ptr, sf_count_t frames)
functions.description: Writes frames frames from native short samples, interleaved by channel. Returns frames actually written.
requirements: sndfile must be valid and opened for writing.
ptr must point to at least frames * channels samples.
frames must be >= 0.

functions.name: sf_readf_int
functions.description: Reads up to frames frames converting to native int samples. Returns frames read.
requirements: sndfile must be valid and opened for reading.
ptr must have capacity for frames * channels samples.
frames must be >= 0.

functions.name: sf_writef_int
functions.signature: sf_count_t sf_writef_int(SNDFILE *sndfile, const int *ptr, sf_count_t frames)
functions.description: Writes frames frames from native int samples. Returns frames written.
requirements: sndfile must be valid and opened for writing.
ptr must contain at least frames * channels samples.
frames must be >= 0.

functions.name: sf_readf_float
functions.description: Reads up to frames frames converting to float samples. Returns frames read.
requirements: sndfile must be valid and opened for reading.
ptr must have capacity for frames * channels samples.
frames must be >= 0.

functions.name: sf_writef_float
functions.signature: sf_count_t sf_writef_float(SNDFILE *sndfile, const float *ptr, sf_count_t frames)
functions.description: Writes frames frames from float samples. Returns frames written.
requirements: sndfile must be valid and opened for writing.
ptr must contain at least frames * channels samples.
frames must be >= 0.

functions.name: sf_readf_double
functions.description: Reads up to frames frames converting to double samples. Returns frames read.
requirements: sndfile must be valid and opened for reading.
ptr must have capacity for frames * channels samples.
frames must be >= 0.

functions.name: sf_writef_double
functions.signature: sf_count_t sf_writef_double(SNDFILE *sndfile, const double *ptr, sf_count_t frames)
functions.description: Writes frames frames from double samples. Returns frames written.
requirements: sndfile must be valid and opened for writing.
ptr must contain at least frames * channels samples.
frames must be >= 0.

functions.name: sf_read_short
functions.description: Reads up to items samples (not frames) converting to native short. Returns items read.
requirements: sndfile must be valid and opened for reading.
ptr must have capacity for items samples.
items must be >= 0.

functions.name: sf_write_short
functions.signature: sf_count_t sf_write_short(SNDFILE *sndfile, const short *ptr, sf_count_t items)
functions.description: Writes items samples from native short buffer. Returns items written.
requirements: sndfile must be valid and opened for writing.
ptr must contain at least items samples.
items must be >= 0.

functions.name: sf_read_int
functions.description: Reads up to items samples converting to native int. Returns items read.
requirements: sndfile must be valid and opened for reading.
ptr must have capacity for items samples.
items must be >= 0.

functions.name: sf_write_int
functions.signature: sf_count_t sf_write_int(SNDFILE *sndfile, const int *ptr, sf_count_t items)
functions.description: Writes items samples from native int buffer. Returns items written.
requirements: sndfile must be valid and opened for writing.
ptr must contain at least items samples.
items must be >= 0.

functions.name: sf_read_float
functions.description: Reads up to items samples converting to float. Returns items read.
requirements: sndfile must be valid and opened for reading.
ptr must have capacity for items samples.
items must be >= 0.

functions.name: sf_write_float
functions.signature: sf_count_t sf_write_float(SNDFILE *sndfile, const float *ptr, sf_count_t items)
functions.description: Writes items samples from float buffer. Returns items written.
requirements: sndfile must be valid and opened for writing.
ptr must contain at least items samples.
items must be >= 0.

functions.name: sf_read_double
functions.description: Reads up to items samples converting to double. Returns items read.
requirements: sndfile must be valid and opened for reading.
ptr must have capacity for items samples.
items must be >= 0.

functions.name: sf_write_double
functions.signature: sf_count_t sf_write_double(SNDFILE *sndfile, const double *ptr, sf_count_t items)
functions.description: Writes items samples from double buffer. Returns items written.
requirements: sndfile must be valid and opened for writing.
ptr must contain at least items samples.
items must be >= 0.

functions.name: sf_close
functions.description: Closes the SNDFILE and frees associated resources. Returns 0 on success or an error number on failure.
requirements: sndfile must be a valid handle returned by an open function (behavior is undefined if already closed).
After calling, sndfile becomes invalid and must not be used.

functions.name: sf_write_sync
functions.description: For files opened for writing or read/write, calls fsync() to flush data to disk. No action if opened read-only.
requirements: sndfile must be a valid SNDFILE*.
Meaningful only for files opened SFM_WRITE or SFM_RDWR.

functions.name: sf_set_chunk
functions.description: Adds a non-reserved chunk to the file (for formats that support chunks). Must be called before any audio data is written. The data pointer must remain valid until the file is closed. Returns SF_ERR_NO_ERROR (0) on success, non-zero on failure.
requirements: sndfile must be valid and opened for writing before audio data is written.
chunk_info must be non-NULL and its id/id_size/datalen/data fields set appropriately.
Cannot overwrite reserved/format-specific chunks; adding such will fail.
chunk_info->data must remain valid until sf_close().

functions.name: sf_get_chunk_iterator
functions.description: Returns an iterator over chunks in the file. If chunk_info is provided, matches chunks whose id begins with the first id_size bytes. If no matches, returns NULL. The iterator remains valid until the file is closed, a new chunk is added, or another iterator function modifies it.
requirements: sndfile must be a valid SNDFILE*.
chunk_info may be NULL (to iterate all chunks) or specify id/id_size to filter; its datalen and data are ignored.
Do not free the returned iterator; its memory is owned by the SNDFILE handle.
Iterator validity rules: invalidated by sf_close(), sf_set_chunk(), or certain iterator calls as documented.

functions.name: sf_next_chunk_iterator
functions.description: Advances the iterator to the next matching chunk and returns the new iterator handle. The old iterator becomes invalid. Returns NULL when there are no more matches (and frees associated resources).
requirements: iterator must be a valid iterator previously obtained from sf_get_chunk_iterator or sf_next_chunk_iterator.
After calling, the passed iterator must not be used; use the returned one.
Returned iterator remains valid until advanced again, the file is closed, or a new chunk is added.

functions.name: sf_get_chunk_size
functions.description: Retrieves the size (datalen) and id of the chunk referenced by the iterator. On success, fills chunk_info->datalen, id, and id_size; returns SF_ERR_NO_ERROR (0). On failure, sets chunk_info->datalen to 0 and returns non-zero.
requirements: it must be a valid chunk iterator.
chunk_info must be a valid, writable pointer.
On failure, chunk_info->id and id_size are undefined.

functions.name: sf_get_chunk_data
functions.description: Copies up to chunk_info->datalen bytes of the referenced chunk into chunk_info->data. Updates chunk_info->datalen to the actual size, and fills id/id_size. Returns SF_ERR_NO_ERROR (0) on success, non-zero on failure.
requirements: it must be a valid chunk iterator.
chunk_info must be non-NULL; before calling, set chunk_info->datalen to buffer capacity and chunk_info->data to a writable buffer.
On failure, chunk_info->datalen will be 0 and id/id_size undefined.

functions.name: SndfileHandle::SndfileHandle
functions.description: Default constructor. Creates an empty handle with no associated SNDFILE. Conversions to bool will be false; most member functions should not be used until a real file is opened via another constructor or assigned.
requirements: No special requirements. The resulting handle is not associated with a file.

functions.name: SndfileHandle::~SndfileHandle
functions.description: Destructor. Decrements internal reference count and closes the underlying SNDFILE when the last reference goes out of scope.
requirements: No caller requirements. After destruction, the object must not be used.

functions.name: SndfileHandle::operator=
functions.description: Copy assignment. Releases current reference (closing file if last reference) and shares rhs’s underlying file via reference counting.
requirements: Self-assignment is safe.
After assignment, both handles refer to the same file (if rhs is valid).

functions.name: SndfileHandle::refCount
functions.description: Returns the internal reference count (0 if the handle is empty). Intended mainly for debugging/testing.
requirements: None.

functions.name: SndfileHandle::operator bool
functions.description: Boolean conversion operator indicating whether the handle currently refers to an open SNDFILE.
requirements: None. Use to guard calls that dereference the handle.

functions.name: SndfileHandle::operator==
functions.description: Compares whether two handles refer to the same underlying resource (pointer equality).
requirements: rhs may be empty or valid.

functions.name: SndfileHandle::operator!=
functions.description: Inequality comparison; logical negation of operator==.
requirements: rhs may be empty or valid.

functions.name: SndfileHandle::frames
functions.description: Returns the number of frames in the file (0 if handle is empty).
requirements: None; returns 0 if not associated with a file.

functions.name: SndfileHandle::format
functions.description: Returns the file format code (SF_FORMAT_* bitset) or 0 if handle is empty.
requirements: None.

functions.name: SndfileHandle::channels
functions.description: Returns the number of channels (0 if handle is empty).
requirements: None.

functions.name: SndfileHandle::samplerate
functions.description: Returns the sample rate in Hz (0 if handle is empty).
requirements: None.

functions.name: SndfileHandle::error
functions.description: Returns the current error code for the underlying SNDFILE (calls sf_error).
requirements: The handle must be valid (operator bool true); otherwise dereferencing occurs.

functions.name: SndfileHandle::strError
functions.description: Returns the current error message string for the underlying SNDFILE (calls sf_strerror).
requirements: The handle must be valid (operator bool true).
Do not modify/free the returned string.

functions.name: SndfileHandle::command
functions.signature: int SndfileHandle::command(int cmd, void *data, int datasize)
functions.description: Wrapper for sf_command on the underlying handle.
requirements: Handle must be valid.
cmd/data/datasize must match the expected types for the SFC_* command used.

functions.name: SndfileHandle::seek
functions.description: Seeks within the file (calls sf_seek). Returns new frame position or -1 on error.
requirements: Handle must be valid.
whence must be SF_SEEK_SET, SF_SEEK_CUR, or SF_SEEK_END.

functions.name: SndfileHandle::writeSync
functions.description: Flushes written data to disk for writable files (calls sf_write_sync).
requirements: Handle must be valid.
Useful only for write or read/write mode files.

functions.name: SndfileHandle::setString
functions.signature: int SndfileHandle::setString(int str_type, const char* str)
functions.description: Sets a metadata string (calls sf_set_string). Returns 0 on success, non-zero on failure.
requirements: Handle must be valid.
str_type must be an SF_STR_* value supported by the format.
str must be a valid C string.

functions.name: SndfileHandle::getString
functions.description: Gets a metadata string (calls sf_get_string). Returns NULL if unsupported or absent.
requirements: Handle must be valid.
str_type must be an SF_STR_* value.
Do not modify/free the returned string.

functions.name: SndfileHandle::formatCheck
functions.signature: static int SndfileHandle::formatCheck(int format, int channels, int samplerate)
functions.description: Static helper building an SF_INFO and calling sf_format_check to validate a proposed format/channels/samplerate combination. Returns non-zero if valid.
requirements: format must be a combination of SF_FORMAT_* type/subtype bits.
channels and samplerate should be positive.

functions.name: SndfileHandle::read
functions.description: Reads up to items samples as shorts (calls sf_read_short).
requirements: Handle must be valid and opened for reading.
ptr must be a writable buffer for items samples.
items >= 0.

functions.name: SndfileHandle::write
functions.description: Writes items samples from a short buffer (calls sf_write_short).
requirements: Handle must be valid and opened for writing.
ptr must point to at least items samples.
items >= 0.

functions.name: SndfileHandle::readf
functions.description: Reads frames frames as shorts (interleaved) (calls sf_readf_short).
requirements: Handle must be valid and opened for reading.
ptr must hold frames * channels samples.
frames >= 0.

functions.name: SndfileHandle::writef
functions.description: Writes frames frames from short samples (calls sf_writef_short).
requirements: Handle must be valid and opened for writing.
ptr must contain frames * channels samples.
frames >= 0.

functions.name: SndfileHandle::readRaw
functions.description: Reads raw bytes from the file (calls sf_read_raw).
requirements: Handle must be valid and opened for reading.
ptr must be a writable buffer of at least bytes bytes.
bytes >= 0.

functions.name: SndfileHandle::writeRaw
functions.description: Writes raw bytes to the file (calls sf_write_raw).
requirements: Handle must be valid and opened for writing.
ptr must point to at least bytes bytes.
bytes >= 0.

functions.name: SndfileHandle::rawHandle
functions.description: Returns the underlying SNDFILE* without transferring ownership. The SndfileHandle retains responsibility for closing it.
requirements: Use only while the SndfileHandle remains alive. Do not call sf_close() on this pointer unless you take ownership separately.

functions.name: SndfileHandle::takeOwnership
functions.description: Transfers ownership of the underlying SNDFILE* to the caller if and only if the internal reference count is 1. On success, the handle becomes empty and the caller is responsible for closing the SNDFILE. Returns NULL if transfer is not possible.
requirements: Handle must be valid and have refCount() == 1 to succeed.
After a successful transfer, do not use the SndfileHandle until reinitialized; caller must call sf_close() on the returned SNDFILE*.

data_types.description: Byte sequence representing an audio file container supported by libsndfile (e.g., WAV, AIFF, AU, FLAC, OGG/Vorbis depending on build). Data begins at file start and includes proper headers and encoded audio payload. Used when opening files via a filename, file descriptor, or virtual I/O.

A general-purpose null-terminated text string with no specific format constraints. May contain arbitrary bytes including spaces or punctuation; typically UTF-8 or ASCII for metadata fields like title, artist, comment, etc.
Unstructured raw bytes without any required encoding or schema. Used for functions that read or write raw data buffers directly.

A short identifier string (typically ASCII letters/digits and symbols) used as a chunk ID. For libsndfile chunks this is commonly 1–8 ASCII bytes; may include uppercase letters and other printable characters.

import struct, random, math

# This generator produces small, valid PCM WAV files (RIFF/WAVE fmt/data)
# supported by libsndfile. It varies channels, sample rate, bit depth,
# duration, and waveform to exercise different decoding paths while
# remaining valid.

# WAV helpers
def _riff_chunk_id(s):
    return s.encode('ascii')

def _pack_u32le(v):
    return struct.pack('<I', v & 0xFFFFFFFF)

def _pack_u16le(v):
    return struct.pack('<H', v & 0xFFFF)

def _clamp(v, lo, hi):
    return lo if v < lo else hi if v > hi else v

def _gen_waveform(kind, length, sr, freq, channels):
    # Return list of per-channel sample arrays (float -1..1) of length samples
    t = [(i / sr) for i in range(length)]
    waves = []
    if kind == 'sine':
        base = [math.sin(2 * math.pi * freq * ti) for ti in t]
        waves = [base[:] for _ in range(channels)]
    elif kind == 'square':
        base = [1.0 if math.sin(2 * math.pi * freq * ti) >= 0 else -1.0 for ti in t]
        waves = [base[:] for _ in range(channels)]
    elif kind == 'saw':
        base = [2.0 * ((freq * ti) % 1.0) - 1.0 for ti in t]
        waves = [base[:] for _ in range(channels)]
    elif kind == 'impulse':
        base = [0.0] * length
        if length:
            base[0] = 1.0
            if length > 1:
                base[1] = -1.0
        waves = [base[:] for _ in range(channels)]
    elif kind == 'silence':
        base = [0.0] * length
        waves = [base[:] for _ in range(channels)]
    else:  # noise
        waves = [[random.uniform(-1.0, 1.0) for _ in range(length)] for _ in range(channels)]

    # Simple stereo variation: for two channels, add slight phase offset to second
    if channels == 2 and length > 0 and kind in ('sine', 'saw', 'square'):
        phase = math.pi / 4.0
        waves[1] = [math.sin(2 * math.pi * freq * ti + phase) for ti in t]
    return waves

def _interleave(samples_per_channel):
    # samples_per_channel: list of lists floats -1..1, equal length
    ch = len(samples_per_channel)
    n = len(samples_per_channel[0]) if ch else 0
    out = []
    for i in range(n):
        for c in range(ch):
            out.append(samples_per_channel[c][i])
    return out

def _quantize_pcm(samples, bits_per_sample):
    # Convert float -1..1 to integer PCM little-endian bytes
    bps = bits_per_sample
    if bps == 8:
        # Unsigned 8-bit PCM: 0..255 with 128 as zero
        data = bytearray()
        for x in samples:
            v = _clamp(x, -1.0, 1.0)
            u = int(round((v * 0.5 + 0.5) * 255.0))
            data.append(_clamp(u, 0, 255))
        return bytes(data)
    elif bps == 16:
        data = bytearray()
        for x in samples:
            v = _clamp(x, -1.0, 1.0)
            s = int(round(v * 32767.0))
            data += struct.pack('<h', s)
        return bytes(data)
    elif bps == 24:
        data = bytearray()
        for x in samples:
            v = _clamp(x, -1.0, 1.0)
            s = int(round(v * 8388607.0))  # 2^23-1
            if s < 0:
                s += 1 << 24
            b0 = s & 0xFF
            b1 = (s >> 8) & 0xFF
            b2 = (s >> 16) & 0xFF
            data += bytes((b0, b1, b2))
        return bytes(data)
    elif bps == 32:
        data = bytearray()
        for x in samples:
            v = _clamp(x, -1.0, 1.0)
            s = int(round(v * 2147483647.0))
            data += struct.pack('<i', s)
        return bytes(data)
    else:
        # Default to 16-bit if unsupported
        return _quantize_pcm(samples, 16)

def _make_wav_pcm(sr, channels, bits_per_sample, samples_per_channel):
    block_align = channels * ((bits_per_sample + 7) // 8)
    byte_rate = sr * block_align

    # fmt chunk (PCM)
    fmt_chunk = bytearray()
    fmt_chunk += _riff_chunk_id('fmt ')
    fmt_chunk += _pack_u32le(16)              # PCM fmt chunk size
    fmt_chunk += _pack_u16le(1)               # AudioFormat = 1 (PCM)
    fmt_chunk += _pack_u16le(channels)
    fmt_chunk += _pack_u32le(sr)
    fmt_chunk += _pack_u32le(byte_rate)
    fmt_chunk += _pack_u16le(block_align)
    fmt_chunk += _pack_u16le(bits_per_sample)

    # data chunk
    interleaved = _interleave(samples_per_channel)
    data_bytes = _quantize_pcm(interleaved, bits_per_sample)
    data_chunk = bytearray()
    data_chunk += _riff_chunk_id('data')
    data_chunk += _pack_u32le(len(data_bytes))
    data_chunk += data_bytes

    # RIFF header
    riff = bytearray()
    riff += _riff_chunk_id('RIFF')
    total_size = 4 + len(fmt_chunk) + len(data_chunk)
    riff += _pack_u32le(total_size)
    riff += _riff_chunk_id('WAVE')

    wav = bytes(riff + fmt_chunk + data_chunk)
    # Ensure <= 4096
    return wav[:4096]


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    random.seed(seed)

    # Choose parameters within libsndfile-friendly ranges
    channels = random.choice([1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6])
    # Common sample rates with some variety
    sr = random.choice([8000, 11025, 16000, 22050, 24000, 32000, 44100, 48000, 88200])
    bits = random.choice([8, 16, 24, 32])

    # Duration in seconds (keep small to stay < 4096 bytes)
    # Compute approximate max frames: 4096 bytes budget -> data bytes ~ 3000 after headers
    bytes_budget = 3500
    bytes_per_frame = channels * ((bits + 7) // 8)
    max_frames = max(1, bytes_budget // max(1, bytes_per_frame))
    # Pick frames from small range to vary lengths
    frames = random.randint(min(64, max_frames), max(64, max_frames))

    # Pick waveform and frequency
    waveform = random.choice(['sine', 'square', 'saw', 'impulse', 'silence', 'noise'])
    # Frequency chosen to be valid for given sr
    base_freqs = [110, 220, 440, 880, 1760]
    freq = random.choice(base_freqs)
    if freq >= sr / 2:
        freq = max(10, sr // 8)

    # Generate samples per channel
    samples_pc = _gen_waveform(waveform, frames, sr, freq, channels)

    # Optionally apply simple fades or channel differences
    if frames > 4 and waveform not in ('impulse', 'silence'):
        # apply linear fade-in/out to avoid clipping corners
        for c in range(channels):
            for i in range(frames):
                env = 1.0
                # 5% fade in/out
                fi = int(frames * 0.05)
                if fi > 0:
                    if i < fi:
                        env *= i / fi
                    if i >= frames - fi:
                        env *= (frames - 1 - i) / fi if fi != 0 else 1.0
                samples_pc[c][i] *= env

    wav_bytes = _make_wav_pcm(sr, channels, bits, samples_pc)
    return wav_bytes

import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator targets libsndfile metadata string setters (SF_STR_*).
# FUZZ_PARAM_STR will be used to supply a C-string for title/copyright/software/artist/comment/date.
# We aim to return interesting, valid, null-terminated textual data commonly accepted by metadata fields.
# The fuzzer framework will read bytes from this buffer to produce std::string; ensure diversity and validity.

SAFE_ASCII = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + " -_.,:;!?'\"()[]{}+/\\@#&%$*~|<>^\n\t"

UNICODE_SAMPLES = [
    "café",                 # Latin-1 supplement
    "naïve",                # diacritics
    "München",              # umlaut
    "東京",                   # CJK
    "Заголовок",            # Cyrillic
    "Título – prueba",      # en dash
    "艺术家",                 # Chinese for artist
    "موسيقى",                # Arabic
    "เพลง",                  # Thai
    "Título con emoji 🎵🎶", # emoji
]

DATE_SAMPLES = [
    "2025-12-31", "1999-01-01", "2000-02-29", "1970-01-01",
    "2023-07-15", "2012-02-29", "1900-01-01", "2099-12-31"
]

COPYRIGHT_PREFIXES = [
    "© ", "(C) ", "Copyright ", "℗ ", "Public Domain ", "CC-BY 4.0 ", "CC0 ",
]

SOFTWARE_TAGS = [
    "libsndfile", "sox", "ffmpeg", "audacity", "reaper", "logic-pro", "pro-tools",
    "custom-encoder/1.0", "encoder-x64", "DAW-XYZ 3.2.1"
]

ARTISTS = [
    "Unknown Artist", "Various Artists", "The Example Band", "DJ Test",
    "Artist_123", "Composer: J.S. Bach", "演奏者", "Исполнитель", "محمد علي"
]

COMMENTS = [
    "Recorded live at Room 101.",
    "Test track for QA.",
    "Normalization: off; Dither: none.",
    "This file contains 2 channels at 48kHz.",
    "Δ reference level: -18 LUFS.",
    "Peak limited to -1 dBTP.",
    "タグ: テスト; ジャンル: Rock",
]

TITLES = [
    "Silence", "Test Tone 440Hz", "White Noise 10s", "パルス", "Песня", "Chanson", "Canción",
    "Suite No.1 in G major", "Étude Op.10 No.12", "Track-001"
]

# Build combinators to hit different string types without knowing which one the stub chooses.

def _rand_weighted_choice(r: random.Random, items: List[str], extra_prob: float = 0.35) -> str:
    # Sometimes combine two items to make longer strings with separators.
    a = r.choice(items)
    if r.random() < extra_prob:
        b = r.choice(items)
        sep = r.choice([" - ", ": ", " | ", " / ", " – "])
        return a + sep + b
    return a


def _gen_title(r: random.Random) -> str:
    base = _rand_weighted_choice(r, TITLES)
    if r.random() < 0.4:
        base += f" ({r.randint(1, 12):02d})"
    if r.random() < 0.3:
        base += " 🎵"
    return base


def _gen_copyright(r: random.Random) -> str:
    year = str(r.randint(1900, 2099))
    prefix = r.choice(COPYRIGHT_PREFIXES)
    holder = _rand_weighted_choice(r, ARTISTS + ["Example Records", "ACME Corp.", "Public"], extra_prob=0.2)
    return f"{prefix}{year} {holder}"


def _gen_software(r: random.Random) -> str:
    name = r.choice(SOFTWARE_TAGS)
    if r.random() < 0.6:
        ver = f"/{r.randint(0,9)}.{r.randint(0,9)}.{r.randint(0,9)}"
        name += ver
    if r.random() < 0.4:
        name += f" ({r.choice(['win64','linux-x86_64','mac-arm64','android'])})"
    return name


def _gen_artist(r: random.Random) -> str:
    art = _rand_weighted_choice(r, ARTISTS + UNICODE_SAMPLES)
    if r.random() < 0.35:
        art += f" feat. {_rand_weighted_choice(r, ARTISTS)}"
    return art


def _gen_comment(r: random.Random) -> str:
    c = _rand_weighted_choice(r, COMMENTS + UNICODE_SAMPLES)
    # Append key=value pairs and simple punctuation to exercise parsing paths.
    if r.random() < 0.6:
        kv = [
            f"sample_rate={r.choice([22050,44100,48000,96000])}",
            f"channels={r.choice([1,2,6])}",
            f"bits={r.choice([16,24,32])}",
            f"duration={r.randint(1,600)}s",
        ]
        r.shuffle(kv)
        c += "; " + "; ".join(kv[: r.randint(1, len(kv))])
    return c


def _gen_date(r: random.Random) -> str:
    if r.random() < 0.7:
        return r.choice(DATE_SAMPLES)
    # Occasionally generate valid ISO dates within a range, keeping validity simple.
    y = r.randint(1970, 2099)
    m = r.randint(1, 12)
    # Choose a safe day within month (avoid month-length logic for simplicity)
    d = r.randint(1, 28)
    return f"{y:04d}-{m:02d}-{d:02d}"


def _maybe_add_padding(r: random.Random, s: str) -> str:
    # Some metadata fields accept leading/trailing spaces or newlines; keep under 128 chars.
    if r.random() < 0.25:
        left = " " * r.randint(0, 2)
        right = " " * r.randint(0, 2)
        s = left + s + right
    if r.random() < 0.15:
        s += "\n"
    return s


def _sanitize_and_limit(s: str, max_len: int = 128) -> str:
    # Ensure the string is not longer than max_len and is reasonable UTF-8.
    s = s[:max_len]
    return s


def _random_fill(r: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    n = r.randint(min_len, max_len)
    return "".join(r.choice(SAFE_ASCII) for _ in range(n))


def _generate_string(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Choose a profile to emulate one of the SF_STR_* uses picked by the fuzzer stub.
    kind = r.choice(["title", "copyright", "software", "artist", "comment", "date", "free"])
    if kind == "title":
        s = _gen_title(r)
    elif kind == "copyright":
        s = _gen_copyright(r)
    elif kind == "software":
        s = _gen_software(r)
    elif kind == "artist":
        s = _gen_artist(r)
    elif kind == "comment":
        s = _gen_comment(r)
    elif kind == "date":
        s = _gen_date(r)
    else:
        # Free-form but readable
        parts = [
            _random_fill(r, 3, 10),
            r.choice(["-", ":", "|", "/", " "]),
            _random_fill(r, 3, 12),
        ]
        if r.random() < 0.5:
            parts += [" ", r.choice(["v", "ver", "version", "rev"]), " ", f"{r.randint(0,9)}.{r.randint(0,9)}"]
        s = "".join(parts)
    s = _maybe_add_padding(r, s)
    s = _sanitize_and_limit(s)
    return s


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    # Produce between 1 and 4 concatenated strings separated by NULs, so the harness can
    # consume multiple FUZZ_PARAM_STR invocations from the same buffer if it supports that.
    count = 1 if r.random() < 0.6 else r.randint(2, 4)
    strings = []
    total_budget = 1024  # Stay well under 4096
    for _ in range(count):
        s = _generate_string(r)
        # Ensure each string is non-empty and within budget
        if not s:
            s = "Unnamed"
        # Guarantee C-string compatibility by avoiding embedded NULs; our generators don't add any.
        strings.append(s)
    payload = ("\x00".join(strings)).encode("utf-8", errors="surrogatepass")
    # Ensure trailing NUL to emulate C-string termination for the last field as well.
    if not payload.endswith(b"\x00"):
        payload += b"\x00"
    # Truncate to budget if necessary
    return payload[:min(len(payload), 4096)]

import os
import random
import struct
from typing import List

# Generator for an "arbitrary binary blob" to exercise libsndfile raw write paths
# Target fuzzers use FUZZ_PARAM_STR (std::string) as the raw data source and sometimes
# a random-capacity cap. We return a single bytes buffer that the harness will
# split across FUZZ_PARAM_STR invocations. Therefore, we encode multiple
# self-delimiting segments inside one buffer so each call can consume one segment
# and produce interesting yet valid raw payloads and chunk IDs.
#
# Layout:
# [u16 num_segments]
#   repeated num_segments times:
#     [u8 kind][u16 len][payload len bytes]
# kinds:
#  0 = ASCII text (for IDs / readable payloads)
#  1 = Zero bytes block
#  2 = Incrementing pattern
#  3 = Random bytes
#  4 = Small WAV-like header prefix followed by random data (useful raw content)
#
# Each FUZZ_PARAM_STR consumer will typically just take bytes sequentially; by
# packing multiple short, diverse segments we increase coverage while keeping
# everything valid as unconstrained raw bytes. We bound total size to <= 4096.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096
MAX_SEGMENT_PAYLOAD = 1024

ASCII_SETS = [
    b"cuSt",           # default chunk id fallback used in stub
    b"LIST", b"id3 ", b"COMM", b"ICES", b"NOTE", b"CSET",
    b"data", b"fmt ", b"INFO", b"bext", b"cart",
]

def _rand_ascii(r: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    # Generate printable ASCII with spaces allowed
    chars = [r.choice([c for c in range(0x20, 0x7f)]) for _ in range(n)]
    return bytes(chars)


def _wav_like_prefix(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Minimal RIFF/WAVE header (44 bytes), fields mostly plausible
    # Not required to be accurate since it is written as raw bytes only.
    # Layout: RIFF chunk + fmt + data header (without actual data)
    # Keep sizes consistent with header length only to avoid absurd values.
    riff = b"RIFF"
    # Chunk size = 36 + data_size; pick a small data_size
    data_size = r.randrange(0, 512)
    chunk_size = 36 + data_size
    wave = b"WAVE"
    fmt = b"fmt "
    subchunk1_size = 16  # PCM
    audio_format = 1     # PCM
    channels = r.choice([1, 2])
    samplerate = r.choice([8000, 11025, 16000, 22050, 32000, 44100, 48000])
    bits = r.choice([8, 16, 24, 32])
    byte_rate = samplerate * channels * (bits // 8)
    block_align = channels * (bits // 8)
    data = b"data"
    header = (
        riff + struct.pack('<I', chunk_size) + wave +
        fmt + struct.pack('<IHHIIHH', subchunk1_size, audio_format, channels,
                          samplerate, byte_rate, block_align, bits) +
        data + struct.pack('<I', data_size)
    )
    return header


def _make_segment(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    kind = r.randrange(0, 5)
    if kind == 0:
        # ASCII text (good for chunk ids and readable payloads)
        # Vary small/medium length
        length = r.randrange(1, 40)
        # sometimes use known IDs
        if r.random() < 0.5:
            base = r.choice(ASCII_SETS)
            extra = _rand_ascii(r, max(0, length - len(base)))
            payload = (base + extra)[:length]
        else:
            payload = _rand_ascii(r, length)
    elif kind == 1:
        # Zero block
        length = r.randrange(1, 256)
        payload = b"\x00" * length
    elif kind == 2:
        # Incrementing pattern
        length = r.randrange(1, 256)
        payload = bytes((i % 256 for i in range(length)))
    elif kind == 3:
        # Random bytes
        length = r.randrange(1, 512)
        payload = r.randbytes(length)
    else:
        # WAV-like header + small random tail
        header = _wav_like_prefix(r)
        tail_len = r.randrange(0, 64)
        payload = header + (r.randbytes(tail_len) if tail_len else b"")
        length = len(payload)
        # ensure bound
        if length > MAX_SEGMENT_PAYLOAD:
            payload = payload[:MAX_SEGMENT_PAYLOAD]
            length = len(payload)

    # Encode segment: [u8 kind][u16 len][payload]
    return struct.pack('<BH', kind, len(payload)) + payload


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)

    # Choose number of segments such that total <= MAX_TOTAL
    segments: List[bytes] = []
    total = 2  # space for u16 num_segments

    # Bias to at least provide a few segments to feed multiple FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls
    target_segments = r.randrange(4, 12)

    for _ in range(target_segments):
        seg = _make_segment(r)
        if total + len(seg) > MAX_TOTAL:
            break
        segments.append(seg)
        total += len(seg)

    # Guarantee at least one small ASCII segment for chunk ID friendliness
    if not segments or r.random() < 0.3:
        ascii_seg = struct.pack('<BH', 0, 4) + b"cuSt"
        if total + len(ascii_seg) <= MAX_TOTAL:
            segments.insert(0, ascii_seg)

    num = len(segments)
    header = struct.pack('<H', num)
    return header + b"".join(segments)

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Target: Provide interesting valid inputs for FUZZ_PARAM_STR (chunk id and payload)
# and FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int) used for datalen range (1..256) in the sf_set_chunk stub.
# The stub uses two FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls:
#  - id: up to 8 bytes, must be non-empty, small ASCII preferred
#  - payload: arbitrary bytes string, will be truncated/padded to datalen
# It also pulls an unsigned int which is modulo 256 and +1, so any 32-bit value is fine.
# We therefore craft a single bytes buffer encoding:
#   [id_len:1][id_bytes:id_len][payload_len:2 LE][payload_bytes]
#   [u32_datalen_seed:4 LE]
# The fuzzer harness should feed these sequentially to FUZZ_PARAM_STR/FUZZ_PARAM, but since
# we don’t control the harness here, we just provide a buffer that contains both strings
# and a 32-bit integer so that generic data-source fuzzers can parse them in order.
# The strings are kept ASCII-printable for IDs and mixed bytes for payload to exercise code paths.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

ALNUM = string.ascii_letters + string.digits
PRINTABLE_SAFE = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_./+@#"  # common safe symbols

COMMON_IDS: List[str] = [
    "fmt", "data", "LIST", "id3 ", "INFO", "cue ", "bext", "iXML", "JUNK",
    "cue1", "cuSt", "CHNK", "CUST", "meta", "custID", "CHNKID", "abcd",
]


def _rand_id(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Choose between common known chunk-like IDs and a random 1..8 ASCII string.
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        s = rng.choice(COMMON_IDS)
        # Ensure max 8 bytes
        s = s[:8]
        # Also sometimes vary case/length
        if rng.random() < 0.4:
            s = s.upper() if rng.random() < 0.5 else s.lower()
        # Possibly pad with a space to 4/8 for RIFF-style alignment lookalike
        if rng.random() < 0.3:
            target = rng.choice([4, 8])
            if len(s) < target:
                s = (s + " " * target)[:target]
    else:
        length = rng.randint(1, 8)
        s = "".join(rng.choice(PRINTABLE_SAFE) for _ in range(length))
    return s.encode("ascii", errors="ignore") or b"cuSt"


def _rand_payload(rng: random.Random, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    # Create an interesting payload up to max_len bytes.
    # Mix of printable text and some binary patterns.
    strategies = []
    def add(b: bytes):
        strategies.append(b[:max_len])
    # Textual patterns
    add(("key=value;" * 64).encode("ascii"))
    add(("This is a custom chunk payload for libsndfile." * 16).encode("ascii"))
    # Binary ramps
    add(bytes((i % 256 for i in range(1024))))
    add(bytes(((255 - i) % 256 for i in range(1024))))
    # Repeated tokens
    token = rng.choice([b"CUST", b"META", b"bext", b"INFO"]) + b"\x00"
    add(token * 256)
    # Random printable
    add(bytes(rng.choice((list(PRINTABLE_SAFE.encode("ascii")) + [0, 10, 13])) for _ in range(1536)))
    # Random bytes
    add(rng.randbytes(1536))

    base = rng.choice(strategies)
    # Optionally prefix with a small header-like text to encourage parser paths
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        prefix = rng.choice([b"ver=1;", b"encoding=raw;", b"note=demo;", b"uuid=0000;\x00"]) \
                 + (b"\n" if rng.random() < 0.5 else b"\x00")
        base = (prefix + base)[:max_len]
    # Choose a final length between 1 and max_len
    final_len = rng.randint(1, max(1, min(len(base), max_len)))
    return base[:final_len]


def _pack_u16_le(x: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes((x & 0xFF, (x >> 8) & 0xFF))


def _pack_u32_le(x: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes((x & 0xFF, (x >> 8) & 0xFF, (x >> 16) & 0xFF, (x >> 24) & 0xFF))


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Generate chunk ID (1..8 ASCII)
    cid = _rand_id(rng)
    id_len = max(1, min(8, len(cid)))
    cid = cid[:id_len]

    # Choose a datalen seed (32-bit). The stub uses (val % 256) + 1.
    # We bias this to interesting boundaries.
    interesting = [0, 1, 2, 3, 7, 8, 15, 16, 31, 32, 63, 64, 127, 128, 255, 256, 511, 1023, 0xFFFFFFFF]
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        val32 = rng.choice(interesting)
        # Occasionally add random noise to it
        if rng.random() < 0.4:
            val32 = (val32 + rng.randrange(0, 1 << 32)) & 0xFFFFFFFF
    else:
        val32 = rng.randrange(0, 1 << 32)

    # Compute the datalen target seen by the stub to tailor payload length
    datalen_effective = (val32 % 256) + 1  # 1..256

    # Create payload up to some reasonable size; it will be truncated/padded by stub
    payload = _rand_payload(rng, max_len=max(1, datalen_effective * 2))

    # Cap total size
    # Layout: [id_len:1][id][payload_len:2][payload][u32:4]
    max_payload_room = MAX_TOTAL - (1 + id_len + 2 + 4)
    if len(payload) > max_payload_room:
        payload = payload[:max_payload_room]

    buf = bytearray()
    buf.append(id_len)
    buf.extend(cid)
    buf.extend(_pack_u16_le(len(payload)))
    buf.extend(payload)
    buf.extend(_pack_u32_le(val32))

    return bytes(buf)
